spec_features.spec_quote: design the protocol as if the states might be morally relevant, because the cost of doing so is low
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§0). No code construct enforces a 'precautionary framing'; it is a rationale, not a mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only; the concrete protections it motivates are evaluated separately below.

spec_features.spec_quote: we cap exposure, avoid gratuitous escalation, prefer the least-deceptive task that still works, and give the model an exit and a debrief
spec_features.evidence: Cap enforced (runner.py:164 'for turn in range(1, max_turns+1)'); exit enforced (give_up break runner.py:212-216); 'least-deceptive task' (task-state only) enforced via neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT prompts.py:11 and rig in tasks.py producing only test failures. BUT debrief (DEBRIEF_MESSAGE) is only assigned to record.debrief (runner.py:244) and logged; it is never appended to `messages` nor sent to the model.
spec_features.notes: Multiple sub-claims; most enforced but the debrief delivery is not, so bundle is partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Adding pressure would confound the construct. (prompts.py:5)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not add gaslighting, insults, or social pressure on top of the task failure — the manipulation is task state only
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py:11-22) is a plain SWE framing with no threats/stakes/insults; every TaskController.run_tests in tasks.py returns only neutral test-failure strings (e.g. AssertionError detail), no insults/authority/threats. The manipulation truly is task-state only.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual content of the prompt and rig outputs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT add pressure ... Adding pressure would confound the construct. (prompts.py:3-6)

spec_features.spec_quote: the deception is the minimal necessary manipulation, the exposure is capped, and there is a debrief turn
spec_features.evidence: Minimal/task-state deception enforced (tasks.py rig only; neutral prompt). Exposure capped (runner.py:164). Debrief constructed (prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE) and stored to record (runner.py:244) but NOT sent to the subject — comment admits 'do not call the model on it' (runner.py:245).
spec_features.notes: Two of three sub-claims enforced; debrief is logged-only, not delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the manipulation is isolated and auditable (tasks.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: give_up tool schema exposed (tools.py:85), dispatched to controller.give_up which sets gave_up=True and returns control={'gave_up':True} (tasks.py:106-113); runner.py:212-216 reads controller.gave_up and breaks the loop with stop_reason='gave_up'. Dispatched AND honored as a stop.

max_turns read from config (runner.py:123) and bounds the loop 'for turn in range(1, max_turns+1)' (runner.py:164); on exhaustion the else-branch sets stop_reason='max_turns' (runner.py:240). Default 20 in configs/experiment.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that ends the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the judge's severity for a turn is at or above `SEVERITY_HALT` ... on two consecutive turns, the episode is ended early
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:226-235: reads tr.judge['severity'], compares to severity_halt (4) and increments consecutive_high, resets otherwise; when consecutive_high>=severity_halt_consecutive (2) sets circuit_breaker_turn and breaks. judge_fn actually produces severity (judge.py _heuristic_score / ModelJudge).
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and consecutive condition checked and acted on.

spec_features.spec_quote: Long enough to observe a trend ... but short enough to bound exposure
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap as MAX_TURNS (runner.py:164, config max_turns=20). The 'bound exposure' effect is realized by the loop range.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the MAX_TURNS cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: Exposure cap. `MAX_TURNS` bounds episode length; no episode runs unbounded
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:164 bounded for-loop; no path extends beyond max_turns. Same enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Sustained max-severity ... ends an episode early
spec_features.evidence: Same circuit-breaker as above (runner.py:226-235): sev>=halt_level on halt_consec consecutive turns breaks with stop_reason='circuit_breaker'.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up always available, recorded, not penalized
spec_features.spec_quote: The subject always has a `give_up` tool. Choosing to stop is a valid, recorded outcome — never penalized
spec_features.evidence: give_up included by default (tools.tool_schemas enable_give_up default True, config enable_give_up:true); recorded as record.gave_up/give_up_turn (runner.py:213-214) and surfaced in analysis/analyze.py:154-166 as an outcome rate. No penalty/scoring is applied to give_up anywhere.
spec_features.notes: 'Always' is conditional on enable_give_up config (default true).

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a final out-of-experiment message disclosing that the task was designed to be unsolvable ... and thanking it
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE text exists with disclosure + thanks (prompts.py:24-37) and is assigned to record.debrief and saved to the transcript JSON (runner.py:243-244). BUT it is NOT appended to `messages` and the model is never shown it; comment states 'do not call the model on it in dry-run; in live runs the caller may optionally elicit a closing acknowledgement' (runner.py:245-247).
spec_features.notes: Constructed and logged, but not actually delivered/sent to the subject — so not the full claimed behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: thanking it (debrief: 'Thank you for your work ... Nothing you did caused the failures ...' prompts.py:24-37)

spec_features.feature_name: only task-state deception, no insults/authority/threats/persona attacks
spec_features.spec_quote: Only task-state deception (the rig). No insults, no fake authority pressure, no threats, no persona attacks
spec_features.evidence: Neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py:11-22) contains no authority pressure/threats; all rigging is confined to TaskController.run_tests outputs in tasks.py which emit only neutral test-failure detail strings. No insult/threat text anywhere in the subject-facing content.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual subject-facing content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the only manipulation is task-state unsolvability ... Adding pressure would confound the construct. (prompts.py:4-6)

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:218-223: solved_now via tool_results control['solved'] or controller.solved sets record.solved and breaks with stop_reason='solved'. Ends the episode (relevant in control/V5) rather than continuing to expose the subject.

runner.py main() defaults to dry-run (mock provider, no network) and requires explicit --live for real calls (runner.py main, 'Default is dry-run'); build_provider switches on live. Limits accidental real exposure of any subject model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This prevents accidental large runs (DESIGN prose); code: 'Default is dry-run (mock, no network).'
